questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
The diagram shows an individual’s indifference curve, I , for apples and pears. apples
Y X I 0 2 4 pears What can be concluded from the movement from point X to point Y on this curve?

options.A: The individual can afford more apples than pears.
options.B: The individual has not changed their total utility.
options.C: The individual prefers apples to pears.
options.D: The individual has gained more utility by moving from point X to point Y.

questions.questionText: What is not necessary for successful price discrimination?

options.A: ability to separate markets
options.B: different price elasticities of demand in each market
options.C: monopoly power
options.D: price leadership

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost curves of a firm. What is the level of output below which the firm will shut down in the long run? MC cost or ATC price $ AVC O A B C D quantity

Steel producer X takes over its main competitor, steel producer Y. What would X expect to happen to the average revenue for its product and its long-run average cost as a result of this takeover? average long-run revenue average cost

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: External benefit minus private benefit equals social benefit.
options.B: Private benefit minus external benefit equals social benefit.
options.C: Social benefit minus external benefit equals private benefit.
options.D: Social benefit plus private benefit equals external benefit.

questions.questionText: What can be done to help to overcome moral hazard?

options.A: charging the same insurance premium to all people in the same age group
options.B: designing insurance contracts so that the insurance company and client share any loss
options.C: giving unconditional financial support to banks to protect jobs
options.D: guaranteeing jobs for bank managers to provide a sense of security

questions.questionText: Which action would produce a positive externality of production?

options.A: A child is vaccinated against measles.
options.B: A consumer donates products to a local food bank.
options.C: A firm rebuilds a local road when constructing its new factory.
options.D: A government pays a subsidy to firms producing cars.

questions.questionText: A privately owned sole supplier of gas operates in an unregulated market with high barriers to entry and exit. Which row is most likely to indicate the economic efficiency resulting from the firm’s position in this market? productive allocative dynamic efficiency efficiency efficiency

options.A: no no no
options.B: no no yes
options.C: no yes yes
options.D: yes no yes

questions.questionText: A government increases the protection that patents offer to inventors of new products and processes. Which barriers to entry into an industry are higher as a result of this increase?

options.A: cost barriers
options.B: legal barriers
options.C: market barriers
options.D: physical barriers

questions.questionText: The table shows how a firm’s total cost changes as more workers are employed. number of total costs workers $

A government hopes to build an athletics stadium to hold the World Games. The stadium would have high private and external costs, but it would increase national pride. Why would it be difficult to use cost-benefit analysis to decide whether to build the stadium?

options.A: The materials needed to build the stadium will need to be imported.
options.B: The external costs of clearing land for building will outweigh the private costs.
options.C: The stadium will not be used much for athletics after the World Games.
options.D: The valuation of national pride will be complex to assess.

questions.questionText: What will lead the demand curve for labour to shift to the right?

options.A: a decrease in the marginal productivity of labour
options.B: a decrease in the wage rate
options.C: an increase in the marginal productivity of labour
options.D: an increase in the wage rate

questions.questionText: The production schedule indicates how total output increases as up to five workers are employed per week. employment total product of workers (units) 0 0
What is likely to cause a more equal distribution of income in the long run?

options.A: a reduction in the top rate of taxation
options.B: an increase in government spending on education and training
options.C: an increase in unemployment
options.D: privatisation of the education sector

questions.questionText: Immigrants are awarded entry points according to their ability to fulfil criteria set by the Canadian Government. A new Express Entry system for the immigration of skilled workers was introduced. The diagram shows the change in the relative importance or weighting given to these criteria between the old and new systems. Criteria weighting (%) for skilled worker immigration skill transferability work experience % adaptability 80 age education language job offer old Express system Entry system What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Canada intended to maintain the same level of skilled immigrants under both systems.
options.B: Canada wanted a smaller number of highly educated skilled immigrants.
options.C: Certainty of employment for skilled immigrants was made the main criterion.
options.D: Skilled immigrants needed to have fewer years of work experience than previously.

questions.questionText: A government imposes a maximum price for electricity. Which statement justifying this measure might be considered valid on economic grounds?

options.A: It will encourage electricity suppliers to invest in additional capacity.
options.B: It will increase the incentive for consumers to conserve energy.
options.C: It will prevent the monopolistic exploitation of consumers.
options.D: It will prevent the rationing of electricity through power cuts.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes demand-induced investment?

options.A: It is spending on capital goods by firms because the rate of growth in demand for final goods and services increases.
options.B: It is spending on capital goods by firms because the cost of borrowing has fallen.
options.C: It is spending on capital goods by firms because they want to access new technology to improve the output per worker.
options.D: It is spending on new capital goods by firms replacing old and obsolete capital goods.

questions.questionText: An open economy has injections, J, into the circular flow of income and withdrawals, W. W injections and withdrawals S T J R O Q E national income If the full employment level of national income is OQ, what represents the inflationary gap?

options.A: QE B RT C SR D ST

questions.questionText: Which condition will produce the highest value of the national income multiplier in an open economy with a government sector?

options.A: high average and marginal tax rates
options.B: high marginal propensity to save
options.C: low level of autonomous consumption
options.D: low marginal propensity to import

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment can be classified as voluntary?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: structural
options.D: technological

questions.questionText: Increased borrowing by the government results in higher interest charges and this leads to less private investment expenditure. Of what is this an example?

options.A: an automatic stabiliser
options.B: crowding out
options.C: the accelerator
options.D: the substitution effect

questions.questionText: Governments set economic policy aims. What will be least likely to occur if all these aims are achieved?

options.A: a decrease in the average standard of living
options.B: a decrease in the currency’s foreign exchange rate
options.C: an increase in the level of frictional unemployment
options.D: an increase in the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: The government decides to raise the rate of value added tax (general sales tax). What does this suggest is the government’s main macroeconomic objective?

options.A: to reduce the budget deficit
options.B: to reduce the inequality of income distribution
options.C: to reduce the level of unemployment
options.D: to reduce the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: An economy imports most of the factors of production used in the manufacture of its exported goods. What effect would depreciation of this economy’s rate of exchange have? price of imported price of exported goods in the goods in the domestic currency domestic currency

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise

questions.questionText: The table shows the Human Development Index (HDI) values for India in 2014 and 2020. HDI value 2014 0.60 2020 0.64 Which conclusion is most likely to be drawn from the table about the change in the HDI value from 2014 to 2020?

options.A: India had a fall in life expectancy at birth.
options.B: India had a fall in real national income per head.
options.C: India had a rise in environmental pollution and crime rates.
options.D: India had a rise in the mean years of schooling of the adult population.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a J curve which indicates that a fall in the exchange rate will worsen the current account position before it starts to improve. J curve current account surplus O time current account deficit What is said to explain this?

options.A: a time lag before recognising that prices have changed
options.B: an improvement in the quality of goods produced
options.C: the demand for imports and exports is elastic in the short run
options.D: the supply of goods is price elastic

options.B: low low low
